places.quote: I think you must have seen that I was struck with those charms on the day when I waited at the Whytorseller.
places.note: Dickens's spelling of the coaching inn Whitehorse Cellar; identification is inferred.

places.quote: upon which she lives in an independent though unassuming manner in the Old Street Road.
My own abode is lodgings at Penton Place, Pentonville.
I have walked up and down of an evening opposite Jellyby’s house only to look upon the bricks that once contained thee.
places.note: Passage names only Jellyby's house; Thavies Inn location comes from the wider novel, so verify.
